chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari, who said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid narrated to us, from his father, from Bakr ibn Salih, from al-Ja'fari, who said: I heard Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) say:
Cut your nails on Tuesday, take a bath on Wednesday, have phlebotomy done for your need on Thursday, and perfume yourselves with your best perfume on Friday.
ai.seo_question: What are the recommended days for cutting nails, bathing, and phlebotomy in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* details a structured weekly routine of physical purification (*taharah*) that mirrors spiritual preparation, culminating in the enhanced grooming for Friday, the day of congregational prayer. By assigning specific acts like nail trimming and cupping to earlier days, it emphasizes the importance of maintaining cleanliness and health as acts of worship leading up to the sacred Friday. This practice reflects the Shia emphasis on *Sunnah* acts that integrate bodily care with spiritual devotion, ensuring one is physically and ritually pure for the weekly gathering.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 7-89 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar quoted Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash’ari, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Bakr ibn Salih, on the authority of Al-Ja’fari that he had heard Abal-Hassan Al-Kadhim (MGB) say, “
Cut your nails off on Tuesdays, go to the bath on Wednesdays and have phlebotomy done on Thursdays if you wish. Put on your best perfume on Fridays.”
